body:
More light, more life. Same layout as beta 8.
• The trackball now lights the window: roll and it warms blue, spin the ring and pink sweeps through, click and amber flashes. It goes still the moment you stop.
• Overview is an instrument cluster: a big live trackball inside three gauges that fill toward your best day.
• Sliders tick as you drag, scroll modes and presets show a little demo when you hover them, and each page has one small moment of its own.
• Panels have depth again, and the type is bigger.
• If the light is too much, Settings › General › Performance › Minimal turns it off.

body:
This one is a new look for the whole app. Your settings are all still here.
• A sidebar, with your trackball at the top. Roll the ball, turn the ring or press a button and it moves with you.
• Every page is redrawn, and each slider now says what its current setting does.
• Settings has five tabs now, including Look & Sound (new soft sounds with one switch, and a choice between the new icon and the classic one).
• After an update you'll see What's New once. It's also under Help.
• New: Settings › General › Allow Raycast and scripts. It's off unless you turn it on.
• If anything looks off or feels worse than before, please tell me. That's what the beta is for.

body: Beta: two new things. (1) About & Help: a new info button at the top of the window (and Glideball › About) opens a sheet with your version, update check, feedback, the welcome tour, helpful links and copyable support info. (2) Show in Dock and app switcher: turn it off in Overview › General to run Glideball purely in the background and reopen it from the menu-bar icon. Tell us how both work for you.
name: Glideball 2.10 beta 1

body: Much lighter on your CPU: Glideball now idles at a few percent instead of 30–50%. The window only animates when something is moving and it's actually visible, and with no trackball connected it stays quiet. New Performance setting (Overview › General): Smoothest, Efficient or Minimal.
name: Glideball 2.9.1

body: Spin the scroll ring harder and the page now goes farther. Glideball used to hit a speed limit at moderate spins, so a very fast spin went no farther than a fast one. A new Fast-spin reach slider (Scrolling tab, Flywheel mode) sets how far the hardest spins fly; turn it to 0% for the old behavior.
name: Glideball 2.9

body: Fixes a trackpad two-finger click being treated as the trackball's right button (it could open Mission Control). Also: Linux and Windows previews are now available on the website.
name: Glideball 2.8.1

body: Glide is now Glideball! Same app, same settings, a name that's easier to find. It renames itself on your Mac automatically — nothing to redo.
name: Glideball 2.8

body: Glide's website has a new, easier address: glideball.netlify.app. The old address keeps working.
name: Glide 2.7.1

body: Automatic backups: Glide now saves a tiny snapshot of your settings every day — kept for two weeks, then monthly for a year — with a timeline on the Sync tab and one-click restore (with Undo). Glide now speaks nine languages: English, Español, Français, Deutsch, Italiano, Português (Brasil), 日本語, 한국어 and 简体中文 — pick one in Overview › General › Language.
name: Glide 2.7

body:
A grand entrance.

- New launch animations: every time you start Glide you get one of six short animations, never the same twice in a row. First-time users get a longer intro with original music, leading into the Welcome Tour. Turn sounds off with 'Launch sounds' in Overview > General.
- Pages now slide between tabs, cards rise in, and today's counters count up.
- Check for Updates: a button in Overview > General, plus 'Check for Updates…' in the Glide menu and the menu-bar menu.
- Choose whether Glide shows its menu-bar icon (Overview > General).
- Fixes: installing an update relaunches properly again, and Glide never holds up logging out, restarting or shutting down.

If an update from 2.3-2.5 seems stuck on 'Restarting…', choose Quit Glide and it will finish installing.
name: Glide 2.6

body:
Combos, shortcuts and a little celebration.

- Three-button combos are easier: tick buttons in the new 'New combo' row (Buttons tab), and pressing three buttons together is more forgiving.
- Keyboard shortcuts (Overview): toggle Precision, Scroll with ball and Drag lock from the keyboard, and change the pause shortcut (Control-Option-Command-G by default). All optional.
- Your trackball: lifetime totals with real-world comparisons, a 7-day chart, personal records and 17 badges to earn, celebrated once with a little confetti.
- 'Make it yours' checklist to set Glide up your way.
- Button ripples and a ring trail on the live trackball, and a 'Saved' check when settings apply.
- Celebrations and sounds can be turned off in Overview > General (sounds are off by default).
name: Glide 2.5

body:
Six new features.

- Precision mode: hold (or toggle) a button to slow the cursor for pixel-perfect aim. Set the precision speed on the Pointer tab.
- Scroll with the ball: hold a button and roll the ball to scroll in any direction while the cursor stays put; let go mid-roll and it glides.
- Drag lock: press once to grab, roll to drag, press again (or click) to drop. No more holding a button while dragging.
- App setups: give any app its own pointer speed, scrolling, buttons and combos. Glide switches the moment that app comes to the front.
- Welcome Tour for new users (Help > Show Welcome Tour).
- Beta program (Overview > General): try Glide with other Kensington trackballs and get early test builds. Off by default.

Safety: pausing (Control-Option-Command-G), quitting or unplugging always undoes precision, ball scrolling and drag lock.
name: Glide 2.4

body:
Send feedback right from Glide.

- Help › Send Feedback… (also in the menu bar menu and on the Overview tab): report a bug, suggest an idea or ask a question, attach screenshots or recordings, and optionally include your Glide settings and scroll log. You see everything that's sent first.
- Or use the website: glide-trackball.netlify.app/feedback
- Bug reports sent after a relaunch now include the previous session's scroll log.
name: Glide 2.3

body:
Polish for one-click updates.

- Glide always checks GitHub fresh, so new versions show up right away.
- The update button is a compact pill that never crowds the top bar.
name: Glide 2.2

body:
One-click updates.

- The Update button now installs new versions in place: it downloads the release, checks it's signed by Glide's developer (tampered downloads are refused), swaps the app and relaunches. Your permissions carry over.
- Lighter on CPU: the Overview graphs use a fraction of the power.
- New Sync tab: nicer export and import with previews and Undo, double-click settings files to open them, and iCloud Drive sync across your Macs.
name: Glide 2.1

body:
First public release of Glide for the Kensington Expert Mouse.

- Pointer speed past macOS's limit, applied only to the Expert Mouse
- Three scroll modes: Native, Flywheel (tuned from Kensington's own driver), Follow
- Remap buttons, two- and three-button combos, quick assign, hold-to-talk shortcuts
- Live dashboard with graphs and an animated trackball
- Backup & Sync: export/import settings files and sync across Macs through iCloud Drive
- Safety: the main click is always a left click; Control-Option-Command-G pauses Glide instantly

Install: unzip, move Glide to Applications, then open it. Because Glide isn't notarized, macOS may ask you to allow it in System Settings > Privacy & Security (Open Anyway). Grant Accessibility and Input Monitoring when asked. Universal: Apple silicon and Intel, macOS 26 or later.
name: Glide 2.0
